knowledge:
- key_parameters: expandGenes=Whether to expand nodes containing multiple paralogues/homologues into individual nodes and copy their edges (essential for gene-oriented analysis and merging) ;; genesOnly=If TRUE, discards non-gene nodes (like compounds) to focus purely on gene product networks ;; pathwayid=The 5-digit KEGG pathway identifier used in retrieveKGML ;; organism=The 3- or 4-letter organism code (e.g., 'hsa' for human, 'mcf' for macaque) used in retrieveKGML
- alternatives: KEGG.db=Neglects graph topology and only provides gene membership ;; keggorth=Does not parse pathway networks ;; cMAP=Specialized only for certain pathways ;; pathRender=Specialized only for certain pathways ;; biomaRt=Alternative for ID translation but requires an active internet connection
- when_to_use: Use when you need to perform graph-theory based analyses (e.g., degree centrality, betweenness centrality) on KEGG pathways, merge multiple pathways to study crosstalk, or subset pathways to focus on specific gene neighborhoods.
- pitfalls: Many disease pathways contain disconnected nodes (degree 0) because KEGG records their involvement but does not provide edges within that specific map; merging related pathways using mergeGraphs can resolve this. ;; When merging graphs, expandGenes=TRUE must be used during parsing to ensure nodes have unique, mergeable KEGG IDs.

workflows.name: pathway_parsing_and_topology_analysis
workflows.intent: Parse a KGML file into a gene-expanded graph and calculate node degrees to identify key regulatory genes.
input: hsa04010.xml (KGML XML file for human MAPK signaling pathway)
workflows.stages: 1. Parse the KGML file into a graphNEL object with gene expansion; 2. Extract node and edge information; 3. Retrieve node-specific KEGG attributes; 4. Calculate in-degrees and out-degrees to identify central regulatory nodes.
workflows.code:
mapkKGML <- system.file("extdata/hsa04010.xml", package="KEGGgraph")
mapkG <- parseKGML2Graph(mapkKGML,expandGenes=TRUE)
mapkNodes <- nodes(mapkG)
mapkEdges <- edges(mapkG)
mapkGnodedata <- getKEGGnodeData(mapkG)
mapkGoutdegrees <- sapply(edges(mapkG), length)
mapkGindegrees <- sapply(inEdges(mapkG), length)
topouts <- sort(mapkGoutdegrees, decreasing=T)
topins <- sort(mapkGindegrees, decreasing=T)

workflows.name: pathway_merging_and_crosstalk
workflows.intent: Merge multiple KEGG pathways to study crosstalk and shared nodes between biological processes.
workflows.stages: 1. Parse individual KGML files into graphs with gene expansion enabled; 2. Combine the parsed graphs into a named list; 3. Merge the graphs into a single unified network.
workflows.code:
mapkKGML <- system.file("extdata/hsa04010.xml", package="KEGGgraph")
mapkG <- parseKGML2Graph(mapkKGML,expandGenes=TRUE)
wntKGML <- system.file("extdata/hsa04310.xml",package="KEGGgraph")
wntG <- parseKGML2Graph(wntKGML,expandGenes=TRUE)
graphs <- list(mapk=mapkG, wnt=wntG)
merged <- mergeGraphs(graphs)

workflows.name: chemical_reaction_network_parsing
workflows.intent: Parse a metabolic pathway to build and analyze a chemical reaction network of compounds.
input: map00260.xml (KGML XML file for Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism)
workflows.stages: 1. Parse the KGML file into a KEGGPathway object; 2. Extract chemical reactions; 3. Convert the pathway into a reaction graph of chemical compounds; 4. Calculate compound out-degrees.
workflows.code:
mapfile <-  system.file("extdata/map00260.xml",package="KEGGgraph")
map <- parseKGML(mapfile)
reactions <- getReactions(map)
chemicalGraph <- KEGGpathway2reactionGraph(map)
outDegrees <- sapply(edges(chemicalGraph), length)

workflows.name: expression_data_integration_and_neighborhood_subsetting
workflows.intent: Map differential expression data onto a KEGG pathway graph and subset the graph to focus on active gene neighborhoods.
input: DE_Colorectal (Named numeric vector of log fold changes with Entrez IDs as names)
ALL_Colorectal (Character vector of all detected Entrez IDs)
workflows.stages: 1. Parse the pathway KGML file into a graph; 2. Translate Entrez IDs to KEGG IDs; 3. Identify upregulated genes; 4. Find the neighborhood of upregulated genes and subset the KEGG graph.
workflows.code:
colFile <- system.file("extdata/hsa05210.xml", package="KEGGgraph")
g <- parseKGML2Graph(colFile)
deKID <- translateGeneID2KEGGID(names(DE_Colorectal))
allKID <- translateGeneID2KEGGID(ALL_Colorectal)
isDiffExp <- nodes(g) %in% deKID
ups <- nodes(g)[logfcs > 0]
upNs <- unique(unlist(neighborhood(g, ups, return.self=TRUE)))
upSub <- subKEGGgraph(upNs, g)
